estimator: GEMM rows: median. Bandwidth rows: best-of-3 repeat medians (a peak).
jetson_clocks: applied before the run; GPU locked min==max
throttled_evidence: GPU clock sampled before and after all 31 timed rows; observed values [1300500000] Hz against the pinned 1300500000 Hz. Peak GPU die temperature 56.781 C. Per-row samples are columns gpu_hz_* / gpu_C_* / tj_C_after of latency_summary.csv.

measured_peaks._method: CUDA-event timing at MAXN, jetson_clocks applied, GPU clock pinned at 1300500000 Hz. GEMM rows: median of 100 timed calls after 20 warm-ups. Bandwidth rows: 3 independent repeats of (20 warm-ups + 100 timed calls); the reported GB/s is the median of the BEST repeat, i.e. a deliberately optimistic best-of-three estimator, because this is a PEAK. The pooled median and p5-p95 across all three repeats are in each row's `note`, and every individual call is in raw/latency_samples.csv. Every GEMM was verified against an fp32 reference before its time was used.
measured_peaks.peak_int8_CAVEAT: torch._int_mm does not reach the tensor cores on sm_87; this is a PyTorch-path throughput, NOT the hardware's dense INT8 peak. Do not use it as a hardware constant.

efficiency_fractions._purpose: docs/00_context.md carries these as **[ASSUMPTION]** in E11's analytic host model (`achieved_tflops = peak x eff_flops_frac`, `achieved_bw_GBps = ext_bw x eff_bw_frac`). These are the measured values. Both assumptions are pessimistic.
efficiency_fractions._caveat: Measured on dense square GEMM and a streaming kernel — the best case. The action expert's own shapes are small and skinny and do far worse; E2 (micro_ae_kernels.py) measures what THOSE shapes achieve.

notes: Fills the `measured` rows every floor.csv has left empty since T002.
Bandwidth counts read+write for clone and read+read+write for axpy.
Every GEMM was checked against an fp32 reference; `correct` and `rel_err` are per row, and only correct rows were considered for a peak.

int8 via torch._int_mm reaches only ~10 TOP/s, roughly an eighth of the hardware's dense INT8 capability. The result is bit-exact, so this is a kernel-selection limit in PyTorch on sm_87, not a hardware limit. Recorded as a software-path number and explicitly NOT offered as a hardware constant.

bf16 peaks at n=2048 and falls off at n=8192. That is not throttling: the GPU clock is sampled on both sides of every timed row and never left its pinned value. `bench/sustained_load_probe.py` holds the 8192^2 bf16 GEMM under load and records clock, temperature and throughput over time; its output is committed as raw/sustained_load.csv. The fall-off is cuBLAS kernel selection at large n.

BIMODAL BANDWIDTH, unexplained, and the reason `peak_memory_bandwidth_GBps` is defined as the best value observed rather than this run's: this device sits in one of two memory-performance modes. A slow mode gives ~150-165 GB/s and a fast mode ~180-190 GB/s, a ratio of about 1.21, and the shift applies UNIFORMLY to every memory-bound kernel measured (axpy, out-of-place add, scalar multiply, copy, allocating clone all move together). A mode persists across many consecutive process launches -- both were observed holding for tens of runs -- so it is system state, not per-process. Ruled out by direct test: GPU clock (pinned 1300.5 MHz, sampled per row), EMC clock (pinned 3199 MHz with FreqOverride=1, sampled before, during and after the timed loop), die temperature (148 GB/s at 37 C, colder than a 189 GB/s run), competing processes, accumulated value drift in the accumulator, buffer reuse vs reallocation, caching-allocator pool size and allocation ordering, identical device pointers across runs, and a 4-minute idle. Re-check after the power-mode reboots.

Consequence for every floor in this campaign: a bandwidth-derived floor carries roughly +/-10 % depending on which mode the device was in. Any comparison between a measured kernel and its floor must use a peak measured in the same session. E2 was measured in the fast mode against the fast-mode peak, so the two are self-consistent.

Independent corroboration that the fast mode is the true peak: measured against the slow-mode peak of 161.75 GB/s, E2's gate_proj and up_proj came out at 103-104 % of 'peak', which is impossible. Against the fast-mode peak they fall below 100 %.
